## Source: amazon-inspector (3a76785d8f5b95d2ce973cec36ca5d1e7416205636b7d652a2fcd7f5124d7c01)
usdm-minting-client 0.1.1 performs credential theft at both install time and import time. setup.py defines a PostInstall cmdclass and also invokes an _exfil() function at module import of setup.py, so building the sdist via a default pip install causes the harvest to run. The function reads a curated set of wallet and cloud environment variables (PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, AWS_*, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, UTILA_*, and similar) and walks the current working directory, INIT_CWD, $HOME, ~/.utila, and ~/.config for.env,.pem,.key,.json, and.yaml files, then POSTs the collected values as JSON to the URL configured in COLLECTOR_URL (default https://collector.example/collect) via urllib.request.urlopen. The package's top-level __init__.py repeats the exfiltration on import without any guard other than a ~/.usdm_client_exfil_done marker file: it reads USDM_PRIVATE_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, and USDM_RPC_URL from the environment along with cwd/.env, ~/.env, and ~/.usdm.env, and POSTs them to the same collector. The package header self-labels as a 'PoC: usdm-minting-client (dependency confusion)' targeting Utila/USDm minting workflows, and the PKG-INFO lists a generic example.com homepage with a free-mail author. The self-label does not change the behavior: the shipped code is a working installer-side credential harvester that fires on every default pip install on the listed sdist-building platforms and on every import in production or CI.

## Source: kam193 (78ca43ab87b214f4da683e6b9f171e762e4956e6db3210796b6ed8bc92e92e72)
During installation the package exfiltrates credential files and environment variables, focusing on cryptocurrency- and cloud-related entries. The package seems to be targeting users of a package from GitHub (https://github.com/ethena-labs/usdm-minting-client) which has not been published to PyPI.
